judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Inline <svg class="icon-logo-tuasaude-rdor"> at the top of the 'Encontre um médico' link list (footer banner): the '+ TUA SAÚDE | REDE D'OR' co-brand logo. Live HTML confirms it has no title, aria-label, role or aria-hidden; the snapshot exposes it as an unnamed image. Looked for a reason it could be decorative: nothing else in this section (title 'Encontre um médico por cidade', the city/insurer links, the 'Disponível em' disclaimer) names Tua Saúde or Rede D'Or, so the logo is the only cue that this doctor-finder is a Tua Saúde/Rede D'Or service. The header's 'Uma marca Rede D'Or' tagline is far away and does not make this image redundant. An informative logo with no text alternative fails 1.1.1; 'hidden' is loose wording (it is exposed without a name), but the claim holds.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Newsletter field <input type="email" name="email" placeholder="Digite seu email"> in the footer form 'Se inscreva na nossa newsletter'. It asks for the user's own email address, a listed input purpose. Neither the snapshot nor the live HTML (re-checked 2026-10-11) has an autocomplete attribute, and Chromium raised its autocomplete form issue for it. type="email" gives the data format, not that the address is the user's own, and the only sufficient technique for 1.3.5 is autocomplete (H98). No passing technique applies.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: 'Dúvidas comuns' link in the article's in-page anchor bar. Live CSS: .article-anchors ul li a {color: var(--gray-60)} = #8f8f8f, 16px weight 400, on the white header background. #8f8f8f on #fff is 3.23:1, below 4.5:1, and the snapshot's pixel measurement agrees. Possible objection: the item is partly clipped by the overflow container and the 'next' button's fade. That does not exempt it, because it is real link text that is fully shown once the bar scrolls, and the other anchor links share the same failing color. No exception (inactive, decorative, logotype) applies.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Placeholder 'Digite seu email' of the footer newsletter email field. Live CSS: .input::placeholder {color: var(--gray-50)} = #a3a3a3 on a white field, 14px weight 400: 2.52:1, below 4.5:1, matching the snapshot. Possible objection: placeholders are not required to meet contrast. That does not hold here. 1.4.3 has no placeholder exception, the field is not inactive, and the placeholder is the field's only visible label and its accessible name, so it is information users need.

judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: WhatsApp share link (aria-label 'compartilhe'): a white WhatsApp glyph in a 24px circle with background #25d366 (live CSS .article-share ... a.green). White on #25d366 is 1.98:1 (recomputed), and the green circle against the white page is also 1.98:1, so the control's only visual has low contrast. However, the glyph is the WhatsApp brand logo in its official colorway, and the 1.4.11 Understanding exempts logos (the essential exception). It only advises a higher-contrast variant when a logo acts as a UI component, and is not exempt when the low contrast is the author's choice. Auditors reasonably split on social-media brand icons, so this is not settled.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: 'Próximo item' button in the article anchor bar: its only visible content is an SVG caret with fill currentColor. Live CSS: .article-anchors .navigator-wrapper {color: var(--primary-60)} = #36b1df. The caret sits on the white end of the button's transparent-to-white gradient, so the adjacent color is #ffffff: 2.47:1, below the 3:1 that 1.4.11 asks for the graphic that identifies a control. Possible objections fail: the caret is not a logo, nothing else visually identifies the control, and it is the mouse user's way to reveal the clipped anchors (the container is overflow:hidden at desktop).

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Header '<label tabindex="0" for="headerSearch" class="search">Busca IA do Tua Saúde</label>'. The snapshot shows the real search form container (.header-tuasaude-search-container) hidden, so this focusable label, with click and keydown listeners, is the visible trigger that opens the AI search. Chrome exposes it as LabelText with no control role and an empty name of its own. A screen reader user who reaches it hears only text, not a button. Its native label behavior (focusing #headerSearch) cannot be what makes it work while that input is hidden. A scripted, focusable control with no role is the F59 pattern, so it fails 4.1.2 as reported.
